.. exception:: InterpolationMissingOptionError

   Exception raised when an option referenced from a value does not exist.
   Subclass of :exc:`InterpolationError`.

   The ``args`` are ``(option, section, rawval, reference)``; the
   attributes are ``option``, ``section``, ``rawval`` and
   ``reference``.

   This error arises when :meth:`~ConfigParser.get` attempts to resolve an
   interpolation reference that does not name an existing option.  Passing
   ``raw=True`` returns the unresolved value instead of raising.  Supplying
   the missing option before calling :meth:`~ConfigParser.get` allows the
   reference to resolve successfully.

   .. doctest::

      >>> import configparser
      >>> cfg = configparser.ConfigParser(
      ...     interpolation=configparser.BasicInterpolation())
      >>> cfg.add_section('sec')
      >>> cfg.set('sec', 'key', 'val %(missing)s')
      >>> cfg.get('sec', 'key', raw=True)
      'val %(missing)s'
      >>> try:
      ...     cfg.get('sec', 'key')
      ... except configparser.InterpolationMissingOptionError as e:
      ...     print(e.option, e.section, e.reference)
      ...     print(e.message)
      ...
      key sec missing
      There is no section named 'sec' or option named 'missing' in...  [reference: 'missing', option: 'key', section: 'sec']
      >>> cfg.set('sec', 'missing', 'X')
      >>> cfg.get('sec', 'key')
      'val X'

   The same applies under :class:`ExtendedInterpolation`, including
   cross-section references of the form ``${section:option}``:

   .. doctest::

      >>> cfg2 = configparser.ConfigParser(
      ...     interpolation=configparser.ExtendedInterpolation())
      >>> cfg2.add_section('a')
      >>> cfg2.add_section('b')
      >>> cfg2.set('a', 'r', '${b:gone}')
      >>> cfg2.get('a', 'r', raw=True)
      '${b:gone}'
      >>> try:
      ...     cfg2.get('a', 'r')
      ... except configparser.InterpolationMissingOptionError as e:
      ...     print(e.option, e.section, e.reference)
      ...
      r a gone
      >>> cfg2.set('b', 'gone', 'Yo')
      >>> cfg2.get('a', 'r')
      'Yo'


.. exception:: InterpolationSyntaxError
